text_blocks.snippet: Residents should report suspicious communications to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of Illinois following a recent alert regarding active phone spoofing scams in the region.
Common Scam Types in Central Illinois

list.snippet: Phone Spoofing: Scammers fake phone numbers to impersonate official entities like the U.S. Attorney's Office. “My office will never stop working to safeguard the citizens of the Central District of Illinois.” -- [U.S. Attorney's Office ].
Utility Slamming: Con artists call local businesses or schools pretending to be with utility providers like Energy Choice or Ameren Choice to trick you into switching electricity carriers.

Fake State & Toll Texts: Fraudulent text messages claim drivers owe money for unpaid tolls, traffic tickets, or fines under threat of license suspension. State agencies never request payments via text message.
Online Shopping & Holiday Scams: Fake websites and social media ads offer hot-topic items or deep discounts to steal credit card data.
Storm Repair Fraud: Transient door-to-door contractors demand large cash deposits or full advance payments following severe weather.
Hang up immediately if a caller makes urgent or threatening demands for money or personal data.
Never click links found in unexpected text messages or emails regarding fines, tolls, or account alerts.
Verify independently by looking up official public numbers rather than using contact details provided by the caller.
Get written estimates from multiple verified local contractors before agreeing to any home repair work.
